institution: Federal Reserve Bank of New York
provider: Federal Reserve Bank of New York
value_date_semantics: effective date of overnight federal funds transactions; EFFR is the volume-weighted median of transaction-level federal funds data
revision_policy: no historical revisions to the effective rate; historical values are stable
methodology_changes: publication time shifted from ~18:00 ET to ~09:00 ET around 2017; value-date settlement convention uses T+1 settlement for the overnight trade date
holiday_handling: no publication on US federal holidays; prior business day convention applies
missing_value_policy: if a publication is delayed, the NY Fed publishes the value as soon as available; no interpolation
machine_readable_format: JSON (also CSV/XML/XLSX/PDF) via the New York Fed Markets Data API
access_requirements: no API key required; public New York Fed Markets Data API
licensing_or_redistribution_restrictions: subject to the Federal Reserve Bank of New York website Terms of Use and reference-rate disclaimers
intended_research_role: primary US overnight benchmark rate for carry calculations
known_limitations: EFFR is unsecured; not comparable to secured benchmarks (SOFR). The NY Fed changed publication time which creates an effective cutover in usability windows around 2017.

institution: Federal Reserve Bank of New York
provider: Federal Reserve Bank of New York
value_date_semantics: same day (T); based on tri-party repo transactions settled T
publication_lag: overnight (value date T, published T+1 morning)
revision_policy: no material methodology changes since inception
methodology_changes: none material; based on actual tri-party repo transactions with a broad panel of dealers
holiday_handling: no publication on US federal holidays
missing_value_policy: if a day is missing (e.g., holiday), no value is assigned; do not interpolate
machine_readable_format: JSON (also CSV/XML/XLSX/PDF) via the New York Fed Markets Data API
access_requirements: no API key required; public New York Fed Markets Data API
licensing_or_redistribution_restrictions: subject to the Federal Reserve Bank of New York website Terms of Use and reference-rate disclaimers
intended_research_role: secondary comparison benchmark to EFFR for assessing secured vs unsecured funding cost differentials
known_limitations: EFFR is unsecured, SOFR is secured — they are NOT interchangeable. Using SOFR as a direct substitute for EFFR in carry calculations systematically distorts the rate differential. The SOFR only exists from 2013-04-03 onward; no pre-2013 SOFR history exists.

value_date_semantics: T-1 (trade date D-1 settlement T-1); based on actual unsecured overnight transactions from a panel of banks
revision_policy: no historical revisions since official start; ECB archives historical €STR alongside EONIA for backward compatibility
methodology_changes: €STR replaced EONIA effective 2019-10-03. EONIA was an average of bank-to-bank unsecured deposit quotes; €STR is transaction-based from a panel of banks. EONIA continued under an €STR-plus-spread methodology until 2022-01-03.
holiday_handling: no publication on EU TARGET holidays; prior business day convention applies
missing_value_policy: if a publication is missing, ECB does not provide interpolated values
machine_readable_format: CSV and JSON via ECB Statistical Data Warehouse (sdw.ecb.europa.eu)
access_requirements: no authentication required for statistical data; public access
licensing_or_redistribution_restrictions: ECB statistical usage terms allow non-commercial use with attribution; no redistribution restrictions for research purposes
intended_research_role: primary EUR overnight benchmark rate for carry calculations from first publication in October 2019 onward
known_limitations: €STR only available from 2019-10-03. Pre-2019 EUR overnight rates must use EONIA, which is methodologically different (quote-based average rather than transaction panel). The panel composition differs between EONIA and €STR, meaning the two series are not perfectly comparable even in the overlapping period.

institution: European Central Bank / European Money Markets Institute (EMMI)
value_date_semantics: T-1 (trade date D-1 settlement T-1); average of unsecured overnight deposit quotes from bank panel
revision_policy: no revisions to historical EONIA values; archived as static historical series
methodology_changes: This record ends with the original EONIA methodology on 2019-09-30. The recalibrated EONIA regime is stored separately and must not be silently spliced to either original EONIA or €STR.
holiday_handling: no publication on EU TARGET holidays
machine_readable_format: CSV and JSON via ECB Statistical Data Warehouse
licensing_or_redistribution_restrictions: ECB statistical terms; non-commercial use with attribution
intended_research_role: primary historical EUR overnight benchmark through 2019-09-30 only
known_limitations: Original EONIA and €STR are methodologically distinct. Do not splice this record to €STR or to recalibrated EONIA without an explicit regime boundary.

institution: European Central Bank / European Money Markets Institute (EMMI)
value_date_semantics: EONIA for the applicable TARGET business day, calculated as €STR plus a fixed spread of 8.5 basis points
publication_time: after €STR publication on the next TARGET business day
revision_policy: archived historical regime; any underlying €STR republication policy applies
methodology_changes: Fixed recalibration: EONIA equals €STR plus 8.5 basis points. This is a distinct regime from original EONIA and from €STR itself.
licensing_or_redistribution_restrictions: ECB/EMMI terms and attribution requirements apply
intended_research_role: diagnostic transition/legacy-contract comparison only; not the primary EUR carry input once €STR is available
known_limitations: This derived benchmark overlaps €STR and must never be silently spliced into the primary EUR panel. Its fixed 8.5 basis-point spread is a methodology regime, not an observed independent funding-rate differential.

benchmark_name: ECB Deposit Facility Rate / Main Refinancing Operations / Lending Facility Rate (policy rates)
frequency: weekly (typically set at monthly Governing Council meetings)
value_date_semantics: effective at the start of the maintenance period following announcement; not a daily observable
publication_time: announcement at Governing Council meeting; no fixed daily publication
publication_lag: N/A — policy rate changes are event-driven, not scheduled daily
revision_policy: policy rates change at Governing Council discretion; no revision to historical rates
methodology_changes: various across policy regimes; negative interest rates introduced 2014; tiering system introduced 2019
machine_readable_format: CSV via ECB website and statistical warehouse
intended_research_role: fallback diagnostic proxy only; NOT a substitute for EONIA or €STR in daily carry calculations
known_limitations: Policy rates are weekly and set by central bank committee decision. They do not represent the overnight market funding rate. Using them as a daily carry proxy conflates monetary policy with actual overnight funding costs. Treat strictly as diagnostic, not as an input to rate-differential carry calculations.

benchmark_name: Sterling Overnight Index Average (SONIA) — reformed methodology
value_date_semantics: T-1 (trade date D-1 settlement T-1); based on actual unsecured overnight transactions
revision_policy: no revisions to historical SONIA values; the original (pre-April 2018) historical series is preserved as-is
methodology_changes: April 2018 methodology reform: SONIA changed from average of quoted unsecured interbank deposits to transaction-based (actual trades). The reformed SONIA series begins 2018-04-02. Both series are preserved, but they are methodologically different and not directly comparable at the April 2018 boundary.
holiday_handling: no publication on UK bank holidays; prior business day convention
machine_readable_format: CSV via Bank of England website and BofE Statistics
access_requirements: no authentication for statistical data; public sector information
licensing_or_redistribution_restrictions: public sector information; free to use with attribution
intended_research_role: primary GBP overnight benchmark for carry calculations
known_limitations: Methodology break at April 2018: pre-reform SONIA (quote-driven, bank panel) vs post-reform SONIA (transaction-based). Both are published as SONIA but are not perfectly comparable. Pre-reform SONIA is suitable for historical backtesting but must be explicitly labelled as pre-April 2018 methodology.

frequency: variable (changed at MPC discretion; typically every 5-8 weeks)
value_date_semantics: effective on the announcement date set by the MPC; not a daily observable
revision_policy: Bank Rate changes at MPC discretion
machine_readable_format: CSV via Bank of England website
licensing_or_redistribution_restrictions: public sector information; free to use with attribution
intended_research_role: fallback diagnostic proxy only; NOT a substitute for SONIA in daily carry calculations
known_limitations: Bank Rate is a weekly policy rate set by the MPC. It is not the overnight funding rate. SONIA is the correct benchmark for daily carry. Bank Rate should only be used as a diagnostic indicator of the general interest rate environment.

benchmark_name: Uncollateralized Overnight Call Rate (TONA) — BOJ main operating rate
value_date_semantics: T-1; based on BOJ uncollateralized overnight call facility transactions
publication_time: next business day (Bank of Japan time, typically morning)
first_available_date: 1979-01-04 (TONA began with the move to the unsecured operating framework)
revision_policy: no revisions to historical TONA values
methodology_changes: Multiple framework changes: pre-1999 administered rates; 1999 onwards TONA as primary operating instrument; 2016 negative interest rate policy (NIRP); 2016 Yield Curve Control (YCC); 2024 transition away from YCC. Each regime change introduces a structural regime break in the interest rate dynamics.
holiday_handling: no publication on Japanese bank holidays
machine_readable_format: CSV via BOJ website and STAT-FINDER (stat-search.boj.or.jp)
intended_research_role: primary JPY overnight benchmark for carry calculations
known_limitations: TONA dynamics differ materially across regimes: pre-2016 positive corridor, 2016-2024 negative rates under NIRP/YCC, post-2024 exit from YCC. Historical data is available but the economic interpretation of the rate differs fundamentally by regime. Yield Curve Control (2016-2024) effectively capped the JPY funding cost at the policy rate, making carry calculations in that period structurally different from a free-market funding environment.

benchmark_name: BOJ Policy Rate (overnight call facility rate / uncollateralized rate)
frequency: daily (but changes at BOJ discretion; not a continuously trading market rate)
value_date_semantics: effective at BOJ announcement; not a market-observed daily rate
publication_time: at BOJ Monetary Policy meeting announcements
intended_research_role: fallback diagnostic proxy only; TONA is the correct daily observable
known_limitations: Policy rate is set at discrete meetings (typically monthly), not observed daily. Using it as a daily carry input ignores the intra-regime dynamics of the actual funding market. TONA is the correct benchmark.

exact_series_identifier: RBA Statistical Table F1 cash rate / AONIA
value_date_semantics: T-1; based on actual overnight unsecured transactions
publication_time: next business day (RBA time, morning Australian Eastern Time)
first_available_date: historical series in RBA Statistical Table F1
revision_policy: official RBA statistical-series revision policy applies
methodology_changes: AONIA is the interbank overnight cash rate published by the RBA; benchmark methodology and historical metadata must be preserved with acquired observations.
holiday_handling: no publication on Australian public holidays; prior business day convention
machine_readable_format: RBA Statistical Table F1 downloadable data
licensing_or_redistribution_restrictions: RBA allows free use of statistical tables with attribution; republication rules apply (must reproduce RBA copyright notice); commercial use requires separate agreement
known_limitations: AONIA is an overnight interbank benchmark proxy, not broker-specific swap/rollover. Preserve RBA attribution and publication metadata.

value_date_semantics: term benchmark fixing for eligible bank bills; not an overnight cash-rate observation
first_available_date: subject to the licensed ASX benchmark-data product and requested tenor
revision_policy: ASX Benchmarks methodology and correction policy applies
methodology_changes: term BBSW methodology is governed separately by ASX Benchmarks and is not the AONIA methodology
missing_value_policy: do not interpolate or substitute for AONIA
access_requirements: separate ASX Benchmarks data access or subscription arrangements may be required; not acquired through RBA Statistical Table F1 as the canonical source
licensing_or_redistribution_restrictions: ASX benchmark-data licensing, usage, and redistribution conditions apply separately; confirm entitlements before storage or redistribution
intended_research_role: diagnostic or forward/term comparison only; not the primary overnight AUD carry input
known_limitations: BBSW is a term bank-bill benchmark, not an overnight financing rate. It must not enter the primary daily carry panel as an AONIA substitute.

frequency: weekly (changed at RBA Board discretion; typically every 5-8 weeks)
value_date_semantics: effective on the declared date; not a daily observable
machine_readable_format: CSV via RBA Statistical Table F1
licensing_or_redistribution_restrictions: RBA statistical terms; attribution required; republication rules apply
intended_research_role: fallback diagnostic proxy only; NOT a substitute for AONIA in daily carry calculations
known_limitations: Cash Rate is a weekly policy rate. It is not the daily overnight funding rate. AONIA is the correct benchmark for daily carry. Cash Rate should only be used as a diagnostic indicator of the monetary policy stance.

benchmark_name: BIS Central Bank Policy Rate Dataset (cross-check reference)
exact_series_identifier: BIS central bank policy rates (country-level weekly series)
value_date_semantics: average policy rate for the week; for long-run comparison and identifying methodological breaks across jurisdictions
publication_time: weekly; next business day after week-end
first_available_date: varies by country; cross-country coverage from 1990s onward
revision_policy: BIS may revise historical policy rate series as countries update reporting
methodology_changes: BIS dataset aggregates policy rates; methodology varies by country and period; useful for identifying breaks but NOT a substitute for overnight transaction benchmarks
licensing_or_redistribution_restrictions: BIS data terms; generally permitted for research with attribution
intended_research_role: cross-check reference for long-run comparison, methodology-break identification, and effective-date verification. Do NOT replace overnight transaction benchmarks with BIS policy rates in carry calculations.
known_limitations: BIS policy rates are weekly averages, not daily transaction rates. They conflate policy decisions with actual market funding costs. They are useful for identifying structural breaks and confirming effective dates but must never silently substitute for an overnight benchmark in a daily panel. The BIS dataset may also contain methodology changes at the country level that require investigation.

institution: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis / FRED
value_date_semantics: previous business day (T-1 settle T); mirror of NY Fed EFFR values
publication_time: available via FRED API when data is published by NY Fed
publication_lag: follows NY Fed EFFR publication schedule
revision_policy: no historical revisions to the effective rate; mirror reflects NY Fed source
methodology_changes: mirrors NY Fed EFFR; no independent methodology
holiday_handling: no publication on US federal holidays; follows NY Fed schedule
missing_value_policy: if a publication is delayed, the NY Fed publishes the value as soon as available; FRED mirrors when available
machine_readable_format: CSV and JSON via FRED API (dailyhistorical endpoint)
access_requirements: no API key required for FRED; public access
licensing_or_redistribution_restrictions: public domain; no restrictions on storage or use
intended_research_role: secondary validation mirror for NY Fed EFFR; NOT the canonical acquisition source
known_limitations: FEDFUNDS is a FRED mirror identifier, not an official New York Fed API series identifier. The canonical acquisition source is the NY Fed Markets Data API with identifier EFFR.
